zh.question: 身体里的细胞如果都长成同样的小圆球，还能做这么多不同的事情吗？
zh.observe: 比较皮肤屏障、骨骼肌纤维和神经元。在肌肉场景先找到两端的连接组织、外部弹簧与固定夹具；同一进度对照允许缩短和固定长度，再改变弹簧刚度。神经场景追踪轴突与突触。切换的是不同观察对象，不是一个细胞变成另一种。

academic.title: 分化把共同基础变成不同本领
academic.body: 很多有核体细胞拥有基本相同的基因组，但表达的基因组合和蛋白质状态不同，形成不同的形态、连接与功能。细胞分化不是仅改变外形，也不表示每种成熟细胞都能随意互换。部分组织靠干细胞或祖细胞补充，更新能力依组织而异。细胞并非只有单一工作，页面挑选的是便于观察的主要功能。

academic.title: 从细胞连接到组织屏障
academic.body: 上皮组织由相接的细胞与连接结构形成连续的层，既可保护，也可承担吸收、分泌等不同功能。皮肤表皮是其中一个例子，角质层的扁平角化细胞及细胞间脂质参与屏障；最外层细胞已失去细胞核。深层活细胞的分裂和分化维持更新。不能把皮肤示意推广为所有上皮都不透物质，也不能把组织视为没有细胞外结构的堆叠。

academic.title: 收缩和传导使用不同机制
academic.body: 骨骼肌纤维是通常多核的长细胞。钙离子调节肌动蛋白与肌球蛋白相互作用，ATP 支持横桥循环；缩短来自细丝滑动，而非细丝变短。产生张力也不必整体缩短。本页用有效收缩元件与外部弹簧的准静态平衡，对照可移动端与固定夹具；总张力含起点预拉，放松回长由外部弹簧牵拉。真实整体等长不保证每个肌节固定，图中肌腱则视为不伸长。神经元的传导依赖膜上离子通道与电化学梯度；髓鞘由胶质细胞形成。本页选择有髓轴突与化学突触。

zh.misconception: 细胞不会因为需要一项工作就立刻换成另一种细胞；肌肉细丝不会自己变短；神经信号也不是一颗小球在空管中流动。
zh.boundary: 三类结构不是人体全部细胞。屏障颗粒、神经亮点、颜色与进度为教学标记。肌肉装置使用屏幕长度、相对力及自选刚度，未校准生理数据；激活改变有效参考长度，不分解真实主动/被动力，不求解横桥、肌腱顺应性、速度依赖、疲劳或主动延长。弹簧刚度不是重量，变硬会减少缩短，但最高档不是过载；不同刚度的初始预伸长也不同。回长来自可见外部弹簧。不由此推断疾病、伤口或实际反应速度。

narration.label: 不同的形状
narration.text: 看一看自己的手。我们看见的是完整的皮肤，放大许多倍，才会看到组成组织的细胞。身体里并不都是一样的小圆球。有些细胞相接成层，有些又细又长，有些伸出许多分支。这些形状和内部结构，都帮助它们完成不同的事情。
narration.cue: 先比较三个观察按钮；停在皮肤的分层画面。

narration.label: 连起来保护
narration.text: 先看皮肤。许多细胞相接排列，形成保护表面。试着推进画面，外面的颗粒遇到完整屏障，停在了外面。皮肤还能帮助身体减少水分流失。最外面的细胞会发生很大变化，深处则有活细胞不断补充。保护工作，是整个组织一起完成的。
narration.cue: 播放屏障过程；指认外部颗粒与深层细胞，留三秒观察。

narration.label: 滑动带来收缩
narration.text: 再看细长的肌肉纤维。先找到左边固定的连接，再找到右边的弹簧。允许右端移动时，推进到中间，肌肉把弹簧拉长，自己变短；放大图里的细丝相对滑动，并没有变短。把弹簧调硬，同样的激活下，缩短会更少。再试固定长度：两端不动，力箭头还是变长了。原来肌肉可以产生张力，却不一定缩短。再回到允许缩短的对照里：激活减弱时，右边的弹簧把它拉回，不是肌肉自己向外推。
narration.cue: 比较可移动端、较硬弹簧与固定端；每次停在同一进度看受力。再切回可移动端，观察放松时的外部回拉。

narration.label: 传信的长长连接
narration.text: 最后追踪神经元的信号。它有分支和长长的轴突，能把信息传到别处。亮点只帮我们找到信号的位置，不是真的小球。在突触那里，细胞还能释放化学信使，把信息交给下一站。神经、肌肉、皮肤和血液互相配合，才让整个身体一起工作。
narration.cue: 切到神经元，先追踪轴突，再停在突触传递终态；结束时回顾分工。

en.question: Could body cells do all their different jobs if they were identical little balls?
en.observe: Compare a skin barrier, skeletal muscle fibres and a neuron. In the muscle study find the connective tissue, external spring and endpoint clamp. Compare shortening and fixed length at the same progress, then change spring stiffness. Follow axon and synapse in the neuron. These are distinct specimens, not one cell changing type.

academic.title: Specialization builds on a shared foundation
academic.body: Many nucleated body cells share essentially the same genome but express different combinations of genes and proteins, developing distinct forms, connections and functions. Differentiation is more than a change of outline and does not make mature cell types freely interchangeable. Some tissues are replenished by stem or progenitor cells, with different capacities for renewal. A cell may perform several tasks; the page selects prominent functions for comparison.

academic.title: Connections create a tissue barrier
academic.body: Epithelia form connected sheets, with roles that may include protection, absorption or secretion. The epidermis is one example: flattened cornified cells and intercellular lipids contribute to its surface barrier, and the outermost cells lack nuclei. Deeper living cells maintain renewal through division and differentiation. This skin model does not imply that every epithelium blocks transport, or that tissue is simply cells piled together without extracellular structures.

academic.title: Contraction and conduction use different mechanisms
academic.body: Skeletal muscle fibres are long and usually multinucleate. Calcium regulates actin–myosin interactions and ATP supports cross-bridge cycling. Shortening comes from filament sliding, not shorter filaments; producing tension need not shorten the whole muscle. This page uses quasi-static balance between an effective contraction element and an external spring, comparing a movable endpoint with a clamp. Total tension includes initial preload, and the external spring restores length as activation falls. Real overall isometry does not fix every sarcomere; model tendons are inextensible. Neuronal conduction depends on membrane ion channels and electrochemical gradients. Glial cells form myelin; the chosen example has a myelinated axon and a chemical synapse.

en.misconception: Cells do not instantly become another cell type to take a job. Muscle filaments do not shorten, and a nerve signal is not a ball flowing through a hollow tube.
en.boundary: These are not all body cells. Particles, signal highlights, colours and progress are teaching choices. The muscle apparatus uses screen lengths, relative forces and chosen stiffnesses, not calibrated physiological data. Activation changes an effective reference length; real active/passive contributions, cross-bridges, tendon compliance, velocity dependence, fatigue and active lengthening are not solved. Stiffness is not weight: increasing it reduces shortening, but the highest setting is not overload. Initial prestretch also varies with stiffness. The visible external spring restores length. No disease, injury or real response-speed prediction is made.

narration.label: Different shapes
narration.text: Look at your hand. We see its surface; magnifying it many times reveals cells in its tissues. The body is not made of identical little balls. Some cells join in layers, some are long and thin, and some have many branches. Their shapes and internal structures help them do different things.
narration.cue: Introduce the three specimen buttons and pause on the layered skin view.

narration.label: Join together to protect
narration.text: Look at skin first. Many cells join into a protective surface. Advance the picture: selected outside particles meet the intact barrier and remain outside. Skin also limits water loss. The outermost cells change greatly, while living cells deeper down replenish them. Protection is the work of a whole tissue.
narration.cue: Play the barrier process; identify outside particles and deeper cells, leaving three seconds for observation.

narration.label: Sliding creates contraction
narration.text: Inspect the long muscle fibres. Find the fixed connection on the left and the spring on the right. With the endpoint free, advance to the middle: muscle shortens and stretches the spring. In the close-up the filaments slide without becoming shorter. A stiffer spring allows less shortening at the same activation. Now fix the length: the endpoints stay still but the force arrows grow. Muscle can produce tension without shortening. Back in the shortening comparison, the external spring restores length as activation falls; the muscle is not pushing outward.
narration.cue: Compare a movable endpoint, a stiffer spring and a fixed endpoint at the same progress. Return to the movable endpoint to inspect external return during relaxation.

narration.label: Long connections carry messages
narration.text: Finally, follow a neuron’s signal. Branches and a long axon help pass information. The bright spot only marks the signal’s position; it is not a real ball. At a synapse, the cell can release chemical messengers that affect the next cell. Nerves, muscles, skin and blood cooperate so the body can work together.
narration.cue: Switch to the neuron, follow the axon, and pause at synaptic transfer; finish by recalling the different jobs.
